mainTopic: The last of the eighteen decrees, and the new משנה on starting work before שבת that continues on שבת
overview: The גמרא finishes listing the eighteen decrees (י״ח דבר) that the Sages made on one day. First, שמואל teaches that produce grown from planted תרומה is also תרומה. רבי חנינא says the worry was a ישראל cheating the כהן, but רבא rejects this and explains that the worry was a כהן holding on to impure תרומה. Next comes the traveler caught on the road when שבת begins, who must give his purse to a גוי. Then the גמרא adds the decrees on the bread, oil, wine, and daughters of non-Jews. It works out a chain in which each decree protects something more serious, ending with a decree that a non-Jewish boy carries the טומאה of a זב. This makes the count eighteen for both רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר. Finally, a new משנה begins: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about starting work before שבת that will continue by itself on שבת. The amud ends in the middle of בית הלל's ruling, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Produce grown from planted תרומה was decreed that same day
steps.stepSummary: טבי the bird hunter quotes שמואל: the rule that גידולי תרומה are תרומה was one of the decrees made on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: טבי the bird hunter said in the name of שמואל: The rule that whatever grows from planted תרומה is itself תרומה was also decreed on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its list of the eighteen decrees. It adds one more: anything that grows from planted תרומה is treated as תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when you plant תרומה, what grows from it is not real תרומה. The Sages made a decree that it does count as תרומה. שמואל says this decree belongs to the famous "that day" of the eighteen decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that grows from planted תרומה
On that very day (the day of the eighteen decrees)

phrases.english: Tavi the bird hunter said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This continues a list from the previous lines, which asked what the other decrees were.

phrases.english: Also, the growths of terumah are terumah,
they decreed this on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבִי רִישְׁבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the listing of the eighteen decrees on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גידולי תרומה are rabbinically considered תרומה, and this was one of the eighteen decrees.

steps.title: Why was this decree made?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree on גידולי תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the Sages were worried about when they made this decree. This short question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rabbinic decree protects against some danger. The גמרא wants to find out exactly what danger this decree was guarding against.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concern led the Sages to treat גידולי תרומה as תרומה?

steps.title: רבי חנינא: the worry is a ישראל holding pure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the decree is because of pure תרומה in the hands of a ישראל, who might plant it to avoid giving it to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: It is a decree because of pure תרומה in the hand of a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question. The Sages feared that a ישראל would plant his תרומה so he could keep the crop for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what grew from planted תרומה were ordinary food, a stingy ישראל could "erase" his obligation by planting the תרומה. Making the growth count as תרומה too removes any gain from this trick.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure תרומה, which a כהן may eat
In the hand of a ישראל (non-כהן)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
It is a decree because of pure terumah
in the hand of a non-kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is that a ישראל would plant pure תרומה to avoid giving it to the כהן.

steps.title: רבא: if we suspect him, he would not separate תרומה at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבי חנינא: if a ישראל is suspected of cheating like this, we should worry he will not separate תרומה in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If they are suspected of this, then they should not even separate תרומה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רבי חנינא's reason. He argues that the suspicion makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who wanted to cheat the כהן would simply skip separating תרומה. Why would he separate it and then go to the trouble of planting it? Since he did separate it, he is plainly not trying to cheat.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If they are suspected of this,
let them also not separate terumah at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דַּחֲשִׁידִי לְהָכִי, אַפְרוֹשֵׁי נָמֵי לָא לַיפְרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's concern about a ישראל holding pure תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we suspect him of wanting to cheat, he would not separate תרומה at all. Since he did separate it, the suspicion falls apart.

steps.title: A ישראל who separates generously can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a ישראל could fulfill his duty with one grain, as שמואל taught. Since he separated more than that, he is trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: A ישראל, since he could have fulfilled the מצוה with a single grain of wheat, as שמואל taught, and he did not do so, is trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his challenge with a strong argument. The ישראל who separates a full portion of תרומה has already shown he is honest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the Torah sets no minimum amount for תרומה, so even one grain would be enough. A person who gives a generous portion when one grain would do is clearly not trying to cheat. So רבי חנינא's worry is rejected.

phrases.english: (Rather, Rava said: a non-kohen,)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

phrases.english: since it is possible to do it with one grain of wheat
as Shmuel taught, and he does not do so,
he is certainly trusted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְמֶעְבַּד חִטָּה אַחַת כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל וְלָא קָעָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבא's challenge and fully rejects רבי חנינא's reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole premise that a ישראל would plant pure תרומה to cheat the כהן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Someone who separates more than the minimum of one grain has already shown he is honest.

steps.title: The real reason: a כהן holding impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reason. The worry is a כהן keeping impure תרומה to plant it, who might later forget and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the decree is because of impure תרומה in the hand of a כהן. Perhaps he will keep it with him, and he will come to a stumbling block.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבא offers his own explanation for the decree. The danger involves a כהן, not a ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not eat impure תרומה. If planting it would produce regular food, he might store it until planting season. Over time he could forget it is impure and eat it. The decree removes his reason to hold onto it.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure תרומה, which may not be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason for the decree on גידולי תרומה is the worry about a כהן holding impure תרומה, not a ישראל avoiding his obligation.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a decree because of
impure terumah in the hand of a kohen,
lest he keep it with him
and come to a stumbling block.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה בְּיַד כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was meant to stop a ישראל from planting pure תרומה to avoid giving it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree stops a כהן from storing impure תרומה, which he might later forget about and eat.

steps.title: The traveler at nightfall gives his purse to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: Another decree from that day, said in the name of עולא: someone caught on the road when שבת begins gives his purse to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other decree: רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: Also, one who was overtaken by darkness on the road gives his purse to a גוי. They decreed this on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the next decree and immediately answers. It adds the rule about a traveler who is still carrying money when שבת starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, he could carry the purse in steps of less than four אמות. The Sages forbade this and told him to hand the purse to a גוי instead. This rule is counted among the eighteen decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the next decree)
It got dark for him on the road (שבת began)

phrases.english: And the other one?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
Also, one for whom it got dark on the road
gives his purse to a non-Jew —
they decreed this on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another decree to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler caught at nightfall on ערב שבת must give his purse to a גוי rather than carry it in short steps. This is one of the eighteen decrees.

steps.title: Non-Jews' bread, oil, wine, and daughters count as one decree
steps.stepSummary: באלי quotes אבימי סנוותאה: the decrees on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine, and daughters all belong to the eighteen decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other decree: באלי said that אבימי סנוותאה said: Their bread, their oil, their wine, and their daughters are all part of the eighteen matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the decrees that separate Jews from non-Jews: their bread, oil, wine, and marrying their daughters. This sets up a counting problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four prohibitions are grouped together here as a single item on the list of eighteen. Because they are counted as one, the total may come up short, and the next step raises exactly that issue.

phrases.english: And the other one?
Bali said that Avimi of Sanvata said:
their bread, their oil, their wine, and their daughters —
all of them are from the eighteen matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, אָמַר בָּאלִי אָמַר אֲבִימִי סִנְוְותָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final item to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decrees on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine, and daughters are part of the eighteen decrees, counted here as one item.

steps.title: According to רבי יוסי, the count is only seventeen
steps.stepSummary: The count works for רבי מאיר. But according to רבי יוסי, there are only seventeen decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי מאיר. But according to רבי יוסי, there are only seventeen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a counting problem. Under רבי יוסי's view, the list falls one short of eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about whether the rule about vessels in the courtyard was one of the decrees. רבי יוסי holds that this dispute was left unresolved, so it does not count. That leaves only seventeen.

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Meir,
but according to Rabbi Yosei, they are seventeen!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי שִׁבְסְרֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the total count after step 8 groups four decrees as one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוסי, the vessels-in-the-courtyard item drops out. With bread, oil, wine, and daughters counted as one, only seventeen remain.

steps.title: Bread and oil are separate decrees, completing eighteen
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אדא, quoting רבי יצחק, teaches that bread was decreed because of oil, and oil because of wine. So these are separate decrees, and the count reaches eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the teaching of רב אחא בר אדא. For רב אחא בר אדא said that רבי יצחק said: They decreed against their bread because of their oil, and against their oil because of their wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the counting problem. It brings a teaching showing that the bread and oil decrees came in separate stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bread was decreed to protect against oil, and oil to protect against wine, each was a separate decree. That adds an item to the list, so even רבי יוסי reaches eighteen.
steps.whatToRemember: This first version of רבי יצחק's chain is challenged in the next step and corrected in step 12. In the final version, bread and oil form one decree, and the missing eighteenth decree for רבי יוסי comes from the 'something else' (the non-Jewish baby) explained in step 14.
steps.confusionAlert: "Bread because of oil" does not mean bread and oil are the same decree. It means each was a separate fence, added one after another.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא הָא דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא.
phrases.english: There is that teaching of Rav Acha bar Adda.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: For Rav Acha bar Adda said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
They decreed against their bread because of their oil,
and against their oil because of their wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא הָא דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one item into separate items
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread, oil, wine, and daughters form a single decree, so רבי יוסי counts only seventeen.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bread and oil were decreed separately, as fences in stages. This adds a decree and completes eighteen.

steps.title: Why would oil be the root of the bread decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק's claim that bread was decreed because of oil. Oil is not more serious than bread, so oil makes no sense as the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: They decreed on their bread because of their oil?! What makes oil stronger than bread?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the chain from step 10. It asks why bread would be forbidden 'because of' oil when oil is no more serious than bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree is made to protect something more serious. Oil of a גוי is itself only a rabbinic decree, just like bread. Nothing about oil makes it a stronger root, so it cannot be what bread is protecting.

keyTerms.meaning: its strength / what makes it stronger

phrases.english: On their bread because of their oil?!
phrases.notes: He's repeating רבי יצחק's chain from step 10, and he's surprised by it.

phrases.english: What makes oil stronger than bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּשֶׁמֶן מִפַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of the chain given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's statement that bread was decreed because of oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A decree must protect something more serious. Oil is not more serious than bread, so oil cannot be the reason for the bread decree.

steps.title: The corrected chain of decrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rebuilds the chain. Bread and oil were decreed because of wine, wine because of daughters, daughters because of 'something else', and that 'something else' because of yet another 'something else'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they decreed on their bread and their oil because of their wine, on their wine because of their daughters, on their daughters because of 'something else', and on 'something else' because of 'something else'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a corrected version of רבי יצחק's teaching. Each decree is a fence protecting the next, more serious thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a גוי's bread and oil leads to drinking together. Drinking together leads to closeness and marriage with their daughters. Marriage leads to 'something else', meaning עבודה זרה (a polite way of not naming it). In this corrected version, bread and oil are now one decree together. So the extra decree רבי יוסי needs must come from the final 'something else', which the next steps identify.

keyTerms.meaning: 'something else', a polite way of referring to עבודה זרה

steps.confusionAlert: 'דבר אחר' appears twice in the last line but does not mean the same thing both times. The first refers to עבודה זרה. The second is a different, still-unknown decree that the גמרא explains next.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גָּזְרוּ עַל פִּתָּן וְשַׁמְנָן מִשּׁוּם יֵינָן,
phrases.english: Rather, they decreed on their bread and their oil because of their wine,
and on their wine because of their daughters,
and on their daughters because of 'something else' (idolatry),

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר אַחֵר מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and on 'something else' because of 'something else'.
phrases.notes: The second 'something else' is not named here. Steps 13–14 explain it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גָּזְרוּ עַל פִּתָּן וְשַׁמְנָן מִשּׁוּם יֵינָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by rearranging the chain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread was decreed because of oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bread and oil were both decreed because of wine, and each link protects a more serious one, ending in a final 'something else'.

steps.title: What is the final 'something else'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the last 'something else' in the chain refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short clarifying question. It sets up the next step, which will name this mystery decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain ended with an unnamed decree. The גמרא needs to identify it to know what it is and how it fits into the count of eighteen.

phrases.english: What is the 'something else'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to explain the last unclear term in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the final decree, called 'something else'.

steps.title: The decree on a non-Jewish baby
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the rabbis decreed that a non-Jewish baby boy carries טומאה like a זב. This keeps Jewish boys from spending too much time with him and being drawn into forbidden male relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They decreed that a non-Jewish baby makes things impure like a זב, so that a Jewish boy should not be used to being with him in forbidden male relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק identifies the mystery decree. A non-Jewish boy is given the status of a זב, even though he never had any discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is distance. If Jewish children know the non-Jewish child makes them impure, they will keep away from him, and that protects against a serious sin. This decree adds a new item to the list, so רבי יוסי's count now reaches eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: the impurity of a זב, a man who had an abnormal discharge
used to being with him, overly familiar

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרוּ עַל תִּינוֹק גּוֹי שֶׁמְטַמֵּא בְּזִיבָה,
phrases.english: They decreed on a non-Jewish baby that he makes things impure like a zav,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא תִּינוֹק יִשְׂרָאֵל רָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
phrases.english: so that a Jewish boy should not be used to being with him
in forbidden male relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק גָּזְרוּ עַל תִּינוֹק גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'something else' is the decree that a non-Jewish baby carries the טומאה of a זב, to keep Jewish boys away from him.

steps.title: Now רבי מאיר has nineteen
steps.stepSummary: If the baby decree is added to the list, then רבי מאיר, who already had eighteen, now reaches nineteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, for רבי מאיר there are also problems: there are nineteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a new problem. Adding the baby decree fixes רבי יוסי's count but breaks רבי מאיר's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רבי מאיר already had exactly eighteen and רבי יוסי only seventeen. The new decree fills רבי יוסי's gap. But it also adds one to רבי מאיר, which gives him nineteen.

phrases.english: If so,
according to Rabbi Meir as well there would be nineteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר נָמֵי תְּשַׁסְרֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new decree from step 14 to raise a counting problem for רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The total count of eighteen according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר already had eighteen. Adding the baby decree makes nineteen, which is more than the known number.

steps.title: רבי מאיר counts two decrees as one
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר counts the decree on foods made impure by liquids and the decree on vessels made impure by liquids as a single decree. So his total stays at eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Foods and vessels that became impure through liquids, he counts them as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר combines two items on the list into one. That leaves room for the baby decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both decrees deal with the same thing: טומאה passed on through liquids. So רבי מאיר treats them as one decree, not two. With that merge, both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי arrive at eighteen.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: bread and oil because of wine, wine because of daughters, daughters because of עבודה זרה, and the baby decree, which completes the eighteen. רבי מאיר reaches eighteen by counting foods and vessels made impure by liquids as one decree.

phrases.english: Foods and vessels that became impure through liquids,
he counts them as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹכָלִין וְכֵלִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְּמַשְׁקִין בַּחֲדָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and closes the discussion of the eighteen decrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר counts foods and vessels as two separate decrees, which would give nineteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר counts them as one, so his total is eighteen.

steps.title: Soaking ink, dyes, and vetch before שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. בית שמאי say you may soak ink, dye plants, or vetch before שבת only if they will finish soaking while it is still day. בית הלל permit it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: You may not soak ink, dyes, or vetch unless they can finish soaking while it is still day. בית הלל permit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its main question is whether you may start a process before שבת that will keep going by itself on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, the work must be completely finished before שבת. According to בית הלל, it is enough that you did your part before שבת, even if the process continues on its own afterward. This first case is soaking things in water.

keyTerms.meaning: vetch, a kind of animal fodder
while it is still day, before שבת starts

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides whether a person must make sure his work is finished before שבת, or only that he himself stops working before שבת. The הלכה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
One may not soak ink, dyes, or vetch
unless there is time for them to soak while it is still day,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין שׁוֹרִין דְּיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. A new משנה starts after the discussion of the eighteen decrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: soaking may begin before שבת only if it finishes by day. בית הלל: permitted.

steps.title: Flax in the oven and wool in the dye pot
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say flax may be put into the oven, and wool into the dye pot, only if they will finish heating or absorbing the dye before שבת. בית הלל permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: You may not put bundles of flax into the oven unless they can heat up while it is still day, and not wool into the dye pot unless it can absorb the color. בית הלל permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more cases of the same argument, this time using heat and dyeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern stays the same. בית שמאי require the process to be done before שבת. בית הלל allow the process to continue by itself. Only the type of work changes here: heating flax and dyeing wool.

keyTerms.meaning: a large pot, here a dyer's kettle

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין אוּנִּין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן לְתוֹךְ הַתַּנּוּר
phrases.english: One may not put bundles of flax into the oven
unless there is time for them to heat while it is still day,
nor the wool into the dyer's kettle
unless there is time for it to absorb the color,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין נוֹתְנִין אוּנִּין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of the same dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: heating flax or dyeing wool must be finished by day. בית הלל: permitted.

steps.title: Setting traps before שבת
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say traps for animals, birds, and fish may be set only if there is time for something to be caught before שבת. בית הלל permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: You may not spread traps for animals, birds, and fish unless they can catch while it is still day. בית הלל permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another example of the same argument, this time about trapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trapping is one of the forbidden kinds of work on שבת. בית שמאי worry about the trap catching something on שבת. בית הלל say setting the trap before שבת is enough, and what happens afterward happens by itself.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹרְסִין מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים
phrases.english: One may not spread traps for animals, birds, and fish
unless there is time for them to be caught while it is still day,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין פּוֹרְסִין מְצוּדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of the same dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: traps only if they will catch by day. בית הלל: permitted.

steps.title: Selling to and loading for a גוי before שבת
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say you may sell to a גוי, help him load, or lift a load onto him before שבת only if he can reach a nearby place before שבת. בית הלל permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: You may not sell to a גוי, load with him, or lift a load onto him unless he can reach a nearby place before שבת. בית הלל permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to cases involving a גוי who will carry things away. The argument stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry here is that the גוי will carry the item on שבת because of what the Jew did. בית שמאי want the גוי to reach a nearby place before שבת starts. בית הלל allow it, since the Jew did his part before שבת.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לְגוֹי וְאֵין טוֹעֲנִין עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: One may not sell to a gentile, nor load with him,
nor lift a load onto him
unless there is time for him to reach a nearby place,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין מוֹכְרִין לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the dispute to dealings with a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only if the גוי can reach a nearby place by day. בית הלל: permitted.

steps.title: Giving work to a non-Jewish tanner or launderer
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say hides may be given to a tanner, and clothes to a non-Jewish launderer, only if the work can be finished before שבת. In all these cases בית הלל permit, and the משנה goes on to add a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: You may not give hides to a tanner, nor clothes to a non-Jewish launderer, unless they can be finished while it is still day. And in all of them בית הלל permit, with…
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case in this part of the משנה. Then comes a summary line saying that in every case בית הלל permit. That line breaks off at the end of the amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי does the work himself, and the Jew only hands it over. בית שמאי still want it finished before שבת. The final word 'עם' ('with') begins a condition that continues on the next daf: 'with the sun', meaning while it is still day.
steps.confusionAlert: This passage ends in the middle of a sentence. 'עם' is the start of 'עם השמש' (with the sun), which comes on the next daf. Do not read 'בית הלל מתירין' here as having no condition at all.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
One may not give hides to a tanner,
nor clothes to a gentile launderer
unless there is time for them to be done while it is still day.
And in all of them Beit Hillel permit, with…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next daf: 'עם השמש' (with the sun).

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין נוֹתְנִין עוֹרוֹת לְעַבְּדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last case of the dispute, followed by a summary of בית הלל's position that continues into the next passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: work given to a non-Jewish tanner or launderer must be finished by day. בית הלל permit in all cases, with a time condition that continues on the next daf.
